claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary tree T with |T|=2p+2 satisfying the route's stated per-selected-tag ordering condition on the component marks of H_v, the complete fixed-selector sum S(T,p) is nonpositive.
claims.scope: First-order shell |T|=2p+2; ordinary finite trees with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1; original supports, neighborhoods, and strict favorable selector; for each selected original leaf, first component mark has H_v-degree at least 2 and the second, if present, has degree at least 1.
claims.reason: retained: The component-root partition and rank shift are exact, the ordering condition forces every residual J_i to have order at most 2k-1, and the independent-set shadow incidence proves each term nonpositive. The zero-extension proof needs the trivial separate case |J_i|<k-1, which is supplied in this critique. Distinct leaves sharing a support retain their multiplicity.

claims.statement: The complete favorable-original-leaf sum is nonpositive for every eligible ordinary tree with |T|=2p+2.
claims.scope: Registered first-order shell: finite ordinary tree T, p with x(T)+2<=p, 3p<2alpha(T)+1, fixed selector F(T,p)={v original leaf: Delta_p(T-v)<0}, and original supports and neighborhoods.
claims.reason: retained: The route correctly leaves the full shell unresolved. The exact first-wide graph classification further shows that an order-2k exceptional residual J_i can be positive only if it has at most one edge, but no argument controls those sparse cases globally or compensates across selected tags.

limitations: The structural root-order condition is not shown to follow from the strict favorable selector.
The first-wide classification narrows possible positive boundary residuals to order-2k graphs with at most one edge, but no global compensation inequality for these residuals is proved.
No full-shell proof, full-sum counterexample, fresh exhaustive computation, external theorem application, or formal verification is supplied.
